recipes.name: Gyeran-guk (Egg Drop Soup)
steps: Boil 3 cups of water with garlic and soy sauce.
Beat the eggs. Slowly pour them into the boiling soup in a circle. Do not stir for 30 seconds.
Add chopped spring onion, salt to taste and a few drops of sesame oil. Turn off the heat.
recipes.notes: Ready in 10 minutes — good when there is no time.

recipes.name: Kongnamul-guk (Bean Sprout Soup)
steps: Rinse the bean sprouts.
Boil 4 cups of water. Add bean sprouts and cook with the lid closed for 7 min (do not open the lid).
Add garlic, soy sauce and salt. Boil 3 min.
Add sliced spring onion and green chilli. Turn off the heat.
recipes.notes: Use mung bean sprouts from the market. Keep the lid closed so the sprouts do not smell raw.

recipes.name: Mu-guk (Korean Radish Soup)
steps: Cut mooli into thin squares (3 cm). Cut chicken into small thin pieces.
Heat sesame oil in a pot. Stir-fry chicken and mooli for 3 min.
Add 4 cups of water and garlic. Boil 15 min on medium heat until the mooli is soft.
Add soy sauce, salt and spring onion. Boil 2 more min.

recipes.name: Sigeumchi-doenjang-guk (Spinach Soybean Paste Soup)
steps: Wash the spinach well and cut in half.
Boil 4 cups of water. Dissolve the doenjang in it.
Add sliced onion and garlic. Boil 5 min.
Add spinach and boil 3 min. Add spring onion and turn off the heat.
recipes.notes: Doenjang is salty — taste before adding any salt.

recipes.name: Baechu-doenjang-guk (Cabbage Soybean Paste Soup)
steps: Cut the cabbage into bite-size pieces.
Boil 4 cups of water and dissolve the doenjang.
Add cabbage, onion and garlic. Boil 12 min until the cabbage is soft.
Add green chilli and spring onion. Boil 2 min.
recipes.notes: Chinese cabbage is best; normal cabbage also works.

recipes.name: Gamja-guk (Potato Soup)
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut into thin half-moons.
Boil 4 cups of water. Add potatoes and garlic. Boil 10 min.
Add sliced onion and soy sauce. Boil 5 min until potatoes are soft.
Add salt, pepper and spring onion.

recipes.name: Dubu-guk (Tofu Clear Soup)
steps: Cut tofu and zucchini into small cubes.
Boil 4 cups of water with garlic and soy sauce.
Add zucchini and boil 5 min. Add tofu and boil 3 min.
Add salt to taste and spring onion.

recipes.name: Kimchi-guk (Kimchi Soup)
steps: Cut the kimchi into small pieces.
Boil 4 cups of water. Add kimchi, onion and garlic. Boil 10 min.
Add tofu, gochugaru and soy sauce. Boil 5 min.
Add spring onion. Taste and add a little salt if needed.
recipes.notes: Lighter than kimchi stew — more water, less oil.

recipes.name: Dak-gomtang (Chicken Soup)
steps: Wash the chicken. Put it in a big pot with 8 cups of water, onion (cut in half), garlic and ginger.
Boil 40 min on medium heat. Remove the foam from the top.
Take out the chicken, tear the meat by hand and put it back.
Add salt and pepper to taste. Serve with chopped spring onion and rice.
recipes.notes: Each person adds salt at the table. Good when someone is sick.

recipes.name: Dakgaejang (Spicy Chicken Soup)
steps: Boil chicken in 6 cups of water for 20 min. Take it out and tear it into thin strips. Keep the water.
Mix the chicken with gochugaru, soy sauce, garlic and sesame oil.
Put the chicken back into the water with sliced onion, bean sprouts and long-cut spring onion. Boil 15 min.
Pour in a beaten egg, wait 30 seconds, then stir gently.

recipes.name: Hobak-guk (Zucchini Soup)
steps: Cut zucchini into thin half-moons.
Boil 4 cups of water with garlic.
Add zucchini and onion. Boil 6 min.
Add fish sauce and salt. Add spring onion.
recipes.notes: No fish sauce? Use 1 tbsp soy sauce.

recipes.name: Saeu-mu-guk (Prawn Radish Soup)
steps: Cut mooli into thin squares.
Boil 4 cups of water with mooli and garlic for 10 min.
Add prawns and boil 3 min (do not overcook).
Add soy sauce, salt, green chilli and spring onion.

recipes.name: Beoseot-guk (Mushroom Clear Soup)
steps: Slice the mushrooms, onion and zucchini.
Boil 4 cups of water with garlic and soy sauce.
Add all vegetables and boil 7 min.
Add salt to taste and spring onion.

recipes.name: Tteok-guk (Rice Cake Soup)
steps: Soak rice cakes in water for 10 min.
Boil chicken in 4 cups of water for 10 min. Tear the chicken into strips.
Add rice cakes, garlic and soy sauce. Boil until the rice cakes float (about 4 min).
Pour in a beaten egg. Add salt and spring onion. Top with crushed seaweed.
recipes.notes: New Year soup in Korea. Rice cakes from the Korean store.

recipes.name: Mandu-guk (Dumpling Soup)
steps: Boil 4 cups of water with garlic and soy sauce.
Add the momos and boil 6 min until they float.
Pour in a beaten egg and stir gently.
Add salt to taste and spring onion.
recipes.notes: Indian chicken momos work well as Korean mandu.

recipes.name: Oi-naengguk (Cold Cucumber Soup)
steps: Cut cucumber into thin strips. Slice onion very thin.
Mix 2 cups of cold water with vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, salt and garlic.
Add cucumber, onion and green chilli. Add ice cubes.
Sprinkle sesame seeds. Serve cold.
recipes.notes: Summer soup — keep it in the fridge.

recipes.name: Miyeok-naengguk (Cold Seaweed Soup)
steps: Soak the dried seaweed for 15 min. Put it in boiling water for 10 seconds, rinse in cold water and squeeze.
Cut seaweed into small pieces. Cut cucumber into thin strips.
Mix 2 cups of cold water with vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, salt and garlic.
Add seaweed and cucumber, add ice and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Maeuntang (Spicy Fish Soup)
steps: Clean the fish pieces with salt water.
Boil 5 cups of water with mooli for 8 min.
Add gochugaru, gochujang, garlic and soy sauce. Add the fish and boil 10 min.
Add zucchini, onion and green chilli. Boil 5 min. Add spring onion.
recipes.notes: Do not stir hard — the fish breaks easily.

recipes.name: Dwaeji-gukbap (Pork and Rice Soup)
steps: Boil pork with onion, garlic and ginger in 6 cups of water for 35 min.
Take out the pork and slice it thin. Keep the soup.
Put rice in a bowl, add pork slices and pour hot soup over.
Add spring onion. Each person adds salt and pepper.
recipes.notes: Serve with kimchi.

recipes.name: Tomato Gyeran-guk (Tomato Egg Soup)
steps: Cut tomatoes into wedges and onion into slices.
Stir-fry tomato and onion with a little oil for 2 min. Add 3 cups of water and boil 5 min.
Add soy sauce, sugar and salt.
Pour in beaten eggs, wait 30 seconds, stir gently. Add spring onion.

recipes.name: Kongnamul-muchim (Bean Sprout Salad)
steps: Boil bean sprouts in salted water for 4 min with the lid closed.
Rinse in cold water and drain well.
Mix with garlic, chopped spring onion, sesame oil, sesame seeds and salt.
recipes.notes: Add 1 tsp gochugaru for a spicy version.

recipes.name: Gamja-jorim (Soy Braised Potatoes)
steps: Peel potatoes and cut into 2 cm cubes. Soak in water 5 min.
Stir-fry potatoes in oil for 3 min.
Add 1 cup of water, soy sauce, sugar and garlic. Simmer 12 min until the sauce is thick.
Add honey and sesame seeds. Mix and turn off.
recipes.notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Gamja-bokkeum (Stir-fried Potato Strips)
steps: Cut potatoes into thin matchsticks. Soak in water 10 min, then drain.
Stir-fry potatoes in oil on medium heat for 5 min.
Add carrot and onion strips. Cook 3 more min.
Add salt and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Gyeran-mari (Rolled Omelette)
steps: Beat eggs with salt. Add very finely chopped carrot and spring onion.
Oil a pan on low heat. Pour in one third of the egg.
When half cooked, roll it to one side. Add more egg and roll again. Repeat.
Rest 2 min, then cut into slices.
recipes.notes: Keep the heat LOW so the outside does not brown.

recipes.name: Hobak-bokkeum (Stir-fried Zucchini)
steps: Cut zucchini into thin half-moons.
Stir-fry with onion and garlic in oil for 4 min.
Add fish sauce (or a pinch of salt). Cook 1 min.
Sprinkle sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Musaengchae (Spicy Radish Salad)
steps: Cut mooli into thin matchsticks.
Mix with gochugaru first so it gets a red colour.
Add garlic, sugar, vinegar, fish sauce, salt and spring onion. Mix well.
Sprinkle sesame seeds.
recipes.notes: Best eaten within 2 days.

recipes.name: Gaji-namul (Seasoned Eggplant)
steps: Cut eggplant into finger-size strips.
Steam for 6 min (or microwave 4 min covered) until soft.
Let it cool a little and tear into thinner strips.
Mix with soy sauce, garlic, spring onion, sesame oil, gochugaru and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Beoseot-bokkeum (Stir-fried Mushrooms)
steps: Slice the mushrooms.
Stir-fry with onion and garlic in oil on high heat for 4 min.
Add soy sauce and cook 1 min.
Add sesame oil and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Danggeun-bokkeum (Stir-fried Carrot)
steps: Cut carrots into thin matchsticks.
Stir-fry with onion in oil for 4 min.
Add salt and sesame seeds.
recipes.notes: Good in lunch boxes and bibimbap.

recipes.name: Yangbaechu-muchim (Cabbage Salad)
steps: Cut cabbage and carrot into very thin strips. Soak in cold water 5 min and drain well.
Mix mayonnaise, ketchup, sugar, vinegar and salt.
Mix the sauce with the vegetables just before serving.

recipes.name: Dubu-buchim (Pan-fried Tofu with Soy Sauce)
steps: Cut tofu into 1 cm slices. Pat dry and sprinkle salt.
Pan-fry in oil on medium heat until golden on both sides.
Mix soy sauce, garlic, spring onion, gochugaru and sesame oil.
Spoon the sauce over the tofu.

recipes.name: Gyeran-jangjorim (Soy Braised Eggs)
steps: Boil eggs for 9 min. Cool in cold water and peel.
Boil 1 cup water, soy sauce, sugar, garlic and green chilli.
Add the eggs and simmer 15 min on low heat, turning them sometimes.
Keep the eggs in the sauce in the fridge.
recipes.notes: Keeps 5 days. One egg per meal with rice.

recipes.name: Dak-jangjorim (Soy Braised Chicken)
steps: Boil chicken in 3 cups of water for 15 min.
Add soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger and green chilli. Simmer 15 min.
Tear the chicken into strips and keep in the sauce.
recipes.notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Gim-muchim (Seasoned Seaweed)
steps: Toast the seaweed sheets in a dry pan for 10 seconds each side.
Put them in a plastic bag and crush into small pieces.
Mix with soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, gochugaru and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Kimchi-bokkeum (Stir-fried Kimchi)
steps: Cut kimchi into small pieces.
Stir-fry kimchi and onion in oil for 5 min.
Add sugar and cook 1 min.
Add sesame oil and sesame seeds.
recipes.notes: Good for old, very sour kimchi.

recipes.name: Hobak-jeon (Zucchini Pancakes)
steps: Cut zucchini into 0.5 cm rounds. Sprinkle salt and wait 5 min.
Dip in flour, then in beaten egg.
Pan-fry on medium-low heat for 2 min each side.
Dipping sauce: soy sauce + vinegar.

recipes.name: Yangpa-jangajji (Soy Pickled Onions)
steps: Cut onions into big squares and put them in a clean glass jar with green chillies.
Boil 0.5 cup water, soy sauce, vinegar and sugar.
Pour the hot liquid over the onions. Close the jar.
Keep at room temperature 1 day, then in the fridge.
recipes.notes: Ready after 2 days. Keeps 3 weeks.

recipes.name: Beurokolli-muchim (Broccoli with Sesame)
steps: Cut broccoli into small florets.
Boil in salted water for 1 min. Rinse in cold water and drain.
Mix with garlic, sesame oil, sesame seeds and salt.

recipes.name: Gamja-salad (Korean Potato Salad)
steps: Boil potatoes and eggs until soft (about 15 min). Peel and mash.
Cut cucumber and carrot into small cubes. Salt the cucumber 5 min and squeeze.
Mix everything with mayonnaise, sugar, salt and pepper.
recipes.notes: Also nice in sandwiches.

recipes.name: Danhobak-jorim (Braised Pumpkin)
steps: Peel the pumpkin and cut into bite-size cubes.
Put in a pan with 0.5 cup water, soy sauce and sugar.
Simmer 12 min until soft and the sauce is thick.
Add honey and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Gyeran-bap (Egg Rice with Soy Sauce)
steps: Fry an egg sunny side up in butter.
Put hot rice in a bowl. Add the egg.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil. Top with crushed seaweed. Mix and eat.
recipes.notes: 5-minute Korean comfort breakfast.

recipes.name: Gilgeori-toast (Korean Street Toast)
steps: Finely shred cabbage, carrot and spring onion. Mix with eggs and a pinch of salt.
Fry the egg mix in butter, shaped like a square the size of the bread.
Toast the bread in butter.
Put the egg and cheese on the bread. Sprinkle sugar, add ketchup and close.

recipes.name: French Toast
steps: Beat eggs, milk and sugar.
Dip each bread slice for 10 seconds.
Fry in butter on medium-low heat for 2 min each side until golden.
Serve with honey.

recipes.name: Omurice (Omelette Rice)
steps: Chop onion, carrot and ham into small pieces. Stir-fry 3 min.
Add rice and 2 tbsp ketchup. Fry 2 min. Put on a plate in an oval shape.
Make a thin omelette with the eggs and salt.
Cover the rice with the omelette. Add ketchup on top.

recipes.name: Dakjuk (Chicken Rice Porridge)
steps: Wash the rice and soak 20 min.
Boil chicken in 4 cups of water 15 min. Tear into strips. Keep the water.
Fry the rice in sesame oil for 2 min. Add the chicken water and cook 15 min, stirring often.
Add chicken, chopped carrot and salt. Cook 5 min. Top with spring onion.
recipes.notes: Good for an upset stomach.

recipes.name: Hobak-juk (Sweet Pumpkin Porridge)
steps: Peel the pumpkin and cut into pieces. Boil in 2 cups of water for 15 min until soft.
Mash or blend until smooth.
Mix rice flour with 4 tbsp water. Stir it into the pumpkin.
Cook 5 min on low heat, stirring. Add sugar and salt.

recipes.name: Yachae-juk (Vegetable Rice Porridge)
steps: Soak rice 20 min. Chop all vegetables very small.
Fry rice and vegetables in sesame oil for 3 min.
Add 4 cups of water. Cook 20 min on low heat, stirring often.
Add salt to taste.

recipes.name: Gyeran-juk (Egg Rice Porridge)
steps: Boil cooked rice in 3 cups of water for 12 min, stirring sometimes.
Pour in beaten eggs and stir.
Add salt, sesame oil and spring onion.
recipes.notes: Uses leftover rice.

recipes.name: Overnight Oats with Banana
steps: Mix oats, milk, curd and honey in a jar.
Close and keep in the fridge overnight.
In the morning add sliced banana.

recipes.name: Banana Pancakes
steps: Mash the bananas. Mix with eggs, flour and milk.
Melt a little butter in a pan on low heat.
Pour small circles of batter. Cook 2 min each side.
Serve with honey.

recipes.name: Vegetable Omelette with Toast
steps: Chop onion, tomato and capsicum small.
Beat eggs with salt and pepper. Add the vegetables.
Cook in oil on medium heat, fold in half.
Serve with toast.

recipes.name: Jumeokbap (Rice Balls)
steps: Chop carrot very small and stir-fry 2 min.
Mix rice with carrot, crushed seaweed, sesame oil, sesame seeds and salt.
Wear gloves and press the rice into small balls.
recipes.notes: Add tuna-mayo inside for a filling.

recipes.name: Chamchi-mayo-deopbap (Tuna Mayo Rice Bowl)
steps: Drain the tuna. Mix with mayonnaise.
Fry an egg.
Put rice in a bowl. Add tuna-mayo, egg and thin onion slices.
Add soy sauce and crushed seaweed on top.

recipes.name: Gyeran-bokkeumbap (Egg Fried Rice)
steps: Heat oil. Fry chopped spring onion 1 min.
Push to one side and scramble the eggs.
Add rice and soy sauce. Fry 3 min on high heat.
Add salt and a few drops of sesame oil.

recipes.name: Avocado Egg Toast
steps: Toast the bread.
Mash avocado with salt and pepper and spread on the toast.
Top with fried or boiled eggs.

recipes.name: Fruit and Curd Bowl
steps: Put curd in a bowl.
Add cut fruit and oats.
Add honey on top.
recipes.notes: Use any fruit in season.

recipes.name: Steamed Sweet Potato and Boiled Eggs
steps: Wash sweet potatoes. Steam or pressure cook (2 whistles) until soft.
Boil eggs for 9 min, then cool in cold water.
Serve with salt for the eggs and a glass of milk.
recipes.notes: Simple Korean diet breakfast.

recipes.name: Gamja-jeon (Potato Pancake)
steps: Grate the potatoes and onion. Do not throw away the starch at the bottom.
Add salt and mix.
Fry thin pancakes in oil on medium heat, 3 min each side until crispy.
Dip in soy sauce + vinegar.

recipes.name: Cheese Tomato Toast
steps: Butter the bread.
Put tomato slices and cheese on the bread.
Toast in a pan with a lid (or oven) until the cheese melts.
Add black pepper.

recipes.name: Peanut Butter Banana Toast
steps: Toast the bread.
Spread peanut butter.
Add banana slices and a little honey.

recipes.name: Dak-bokkeumtang (Spicy Braised Chicken)
steps: Boil chicken pieces in water 3 min, then rinse (this cleans the chicken).
Mix gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic.
Put chicken, sauce and 2 cups of water in a pot. Boil 15 min.
Add big pieces of potato, carrot and onion. Cook 15 min until the potatoes are soft.
Add green chilli and spring onion.

recipes.name: Jjimdak (Soy Braised Chicken with Glass Noodles)
steps: Soak glass noodles in warm water 30 min.
Boil chicken in water 3 min and rinse.
Cook chicken with 2.5 cups water, soy sauce, sugar, oyster sauce and garlic for 15 min.
Add potato, carrot and onion. Cook 12 min.
Add glass noodles and green chilli. Cook 3 min until noodles are soft. Add spring onion.

recipes.name: Dakgangjeong (Sweet Crispy Chicken)
steps: Cut chicken into bite-size pieces. Mix with salt and pepper.
Coat with corn flour. Deep-fry 6 min. Rest 2 min and fry again 2 min (extra crispy).
In a pan boil soy sauce, ketchup, honey, gochujang and garlic for 2 min.
Toss the chicken in the sauce. Sprinkle sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Ganjang-chicken (Soy Garlic Chicken)
steps: Cut chicken into pieces. Pan-fry skin side down until golden.
Remove extra oil. Add soy sauce, sugar, honey, garlic and 0.5 cup water.
Simmer 10 min until the sauce is sticky.
Add sliced green chilli and spring onion.

recipes.name: Chicken Katsu with Cabbage Salad
steps: Cut chicken breast in half (thin). Hit with a rolling pin. Add salt and pepper.
Coat with flour, then egg, then bread crumbs.
Deep-fry on medium heat 4 min each side until golden.
Sauce: ketchup + BBQ sauce. Serve with thin cabbage and mayonnaise.

recipes.name: Dak-kkochi (Chicken Skewers)
steps: Cut chicken and spring onion into 3 cm pieces. Put them on skewers.
Mix soy sauce, sugar, honey, garlic and gochujang.
Pan-fry skewers in oil 8 min, turning.
Brush the sauce on and cook 2 more min.

recipes.name: Dubu-kimchi (Tofu with Stir-fried Kimchi)
steps: Boil the tofu block 3 min. Cut into thick slices.
Stir-fry pork in oil 3 min. Add kimchi and onion. Fry 5 min.
Add gochujang and sugar. Fry 2 min. Add sesame oil and seeds.
Put tofu around the plate and kimchi in the middle.
recipes.notes: Vegetarian: skip the pork.

recipes.name: Mapa-dubu (Korean Mapo Tofu)
steps: Cut tofu into cubes. Mince the chicken.
Fry chicken, onion, garlic and ginger 3 min.
Add 1 cup water, gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce and oyster sauce. Boil.
Add tofu and cook 4 min. Add corn flour mixed with 2 tbsp water to thicken. Add spring onion.
recipes.notes: Serve on rice.

recipes.name: Japchae (Glass Noodle Stir-fry)
steps: Boil glass noodles 6 min. Drain and cut with scissors.
Blanch spinach 30 seconds and squeeze.
Stir-fry onion, carrot, capsicum and mushrooms separately with a little oil and salt.
Mix noodles with soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and garlic in a big pan for 2 min.
Add all vegetables and mix. Sprinkle sesame seeds.
recipes.notes: Vegetarian main. Add chicken strips if you like.

recipes.name: Bibimbap (Mixed Rice with Vegetables)
steps: Blanch bean sprouts and spinach. Season each with salt and sesame oil.
Stir-fry carrot and zucchini strips separately with a little salt.
Fry the eggs sunny side up.
Put rice in bowls, arrange the vegetables on top, add egg.
Serve with gochujang and sesame oil. Mix before eating.

recipes.name: Ganjang-saeu-bokkeum (Garlic Soy Prawns)
steps: Pat the prawns dry.
Melt butter. Fry garlic 30 seconds.
Add prawns and cook 2 min each side.
Add soy sauce, sugar and honey. Cook 1 min. Add spring onion.

recipes.name: Kkanpung-saeu (Sweet Spicy Garlic Prawns)
steps: Coat prawns with corn flour and fry until crispy.
In another pan fry garlic, green chilli and capsicum 1 min.
Add soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, ketchup and 3 tbsp water. Boil 1 min.
Add the prawns and toss quickly.

recipes.name: Godeungeo-jorim (Braised Mackerel with Radish)
steps: Clean the mackerel and cut into 3 pieces each.
Put thick mooli slices at the bottom of a pan. Put the fish on top.
Mix soy sauce, gochugaru, sugar, garlic, ginger and 1 cup water. Pour over.
Cover and cook 20 min on medium heat, spooning sauce over. Add onion, chilli, spring onion for the last 5 min.
recipes.notes: Bangda is cheap and good in Pune fish markets.

recipes.name: Saengseon-gui (Pan-fried Pomfret)
steps: Clean the fish and make 2 cuts on each side. Sprinkle salt and rest 10 min.
Pat dry and dust with a little flour.
Pan-fry in oil on medium heat 5 min each side until golden.
Serve with lemon.
recipes.notes: Surmai slices also work.

recipes.name: Ojingeo-bokkeum (Spicy Stir-fried Squid)
steps: Cut squid into rings or strips.
Mix gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic.
Stir-fry vegetables in oil on high heat 2 min.
Add squid and sauce. Cook only 2-3 min (more makes it hard). Add sesame oil.

recipes.name: Suyuk (Boiled Pork Belly with Kimchi)
steps: Put pork in a pot with water to cover, onion, garlic, ginger and doenjang.
Boil 40 min on medium heat.
Rest 5 min and slice thin.
Serve with kimchi and lettuce leaves for wrapping.

recipes.name: Dwaeji-bulgogi (Soy Pork Bulgogi)
steps: Mix soy sauce, sugar, garlic, sesame oil and pepper. Marinate the pork 20 min.
Stir-fry on high heat 5 min.
Add onion and carrot. Cook 3 min. Add spring onion.
recipes.notes: Not spicy — good with lettuce wraps.

recipes.name: Paneer Bulgogi
steps: Cut paneer into thick strips.
Mix soy sauce, sugar, honey, garlic and sesame oil.
Pan-fry paneer until light golden. Add onion and capsicum, cook 2 min.
Add the sauce and toss 1 min. Sprinkle sesame seeds.
recipes.notes: Vegetarian main with Korean taste.

recipes.name: Haemul-pajeon (Seafood Spring Onion Pancake)
steps: Mix flour, 0.8 cup cold water, egg and salt.
Cut spring onion into long pieces. Chop the seafood small.
Put spring onion in an oiled pan, pour batter and seafood over.
Cook on medium heat 4 min each side until crispy.
Dipping sauce: soy sauce + vinegar.

recipes.name: Tteokbokki (Spicy Rice Cakes)
steps: Soak rice cakes 10 min. Boil the eggs 9 min and peel.
Boil 2 cups water with gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce and sugar.
Add rice cakes, cabbage and onion. Cook 8 min, stirring, until the sauce is thick.
Add boiled eggs and spring onion.
recipes.notes: Korean street food. Rice cakes from the Korean store.

recipes.name: Nurungji (Crispy Scorched Rice)
steps: Spread a very thin layer of oil in a non-stick pan (or use no oil).
Put the cooked rice in the pan. Press it flat and thin (about 3 mm) with a wet spoon.
Cook on LOW heat for 15–20 min without moving it, until the bottom is golden and crispy.
Turn it over and cook 5 more min. Let it cool on a plate — it becomes hard and crispy.
To eat as a snack: break into pieces (sprinkle a little sugar if you like).
For breakfast (nurungji-tang): boil 1 piece with 2 cups of water for 8–10 min until soft. Serve hot with kimchi and side dishes.
recipes.notes: Use leftover rice. Keeps 2 weeks in a dry airtight box.
